profile.campus_mw_context: The 128,715-sq. ft. data center in Sterling, VA, offers 11 MW of IT capacity and features robust connectivity options with high bandwidth and high-availability circuits and a number of metro and long-haul networks.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA4 in Sterling, Virginia offers 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet, ranking 26th among Virginia facilities with published capacity and less than 1% of the state's disclosed total.

The facility's 11 MW translates to roughly 275 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density. That is modest relative to the 1,603 MW disclosed across Virginia's 25 reporting data centers. Its emphasis on multiple metro and long-haul circuits points to data movement rather than raw power as the design priority, which suits distributed inference or enterprise workloads more than frontier training.

The data does not show whether this site can support large-scale training runs, because it publishes no power credentials beyond IT load. Virginia has 330 mapped data centers, but 305 publish no capacity, so the state's true aggregate AI infrastructure remains unknown. This facility's role in AI scaling depends on what those unpublished campuses contain.
